subject: Trial playbook and evaluation framework — Redwood / NovaDocs
thread_summary: Post-demo recap and alignment on success criteria, proposed trial plan (two-week trial + optional shadow run), evaluation methodology (offline scoring vs online shadow), grading rubric, timelines, and ownership.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@novadocs.ai>, NovaDocs Evaluation Team <eval@novadocs.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Trial playbook and evaluation framework — Redwood / NovaDocs

Hi Ibrahim + NovaDocs team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the open conversation about your ingestion patterns and the compliance constraints around PHI redaction. As promised, here’s a concise recap and a proposed trial playbook to keep momentum.

Key goals (from today's discovery):
- Improve document classification accuracy for legal/consent labels from ~78% -> target >= 92% on production-ish data.
- Reduce median inference latency for interactive review flows to <= 350ms for 512-token requests.
- Verify token cost at expected volumes (50k tokens/day) and estimate monthly spend.

Proposed trial structure (2 weeks + optional shadow week):
1) Week 0 (setup, 3 business days): environment onboarding, dataset ingest (anonymized sample), access to encrypted logs, and baseline run.
2) Week 1-2 (run + offline eval): run on a reserved Dedicated slot (config T4x2), collect outputs, run offline evals with your rubric and our eval harness.
3) Optional Week 3 (online shadow): mirror live traffic in read-only mode for 72h to measure latencies and KV-cache behavior before any production cuts.

Success criteria (initial proposal):
- Classification F1 >= 0.92 on labelled evaluation set (per-class min 0.88).
- Precision on PHI-redaction >= 0.995 (false negatives intolerable).
- Median P50 latency <= 350ms; P95 <= 900ms under expected burst profile.
- Unit token cost <= $0.009 at the configured batching profile.

Open questions for you (please confirm):
- Can you provide an anonymized sample of 10k documents by end of day Monday (or earlier)?
- Will the legal team sign the attached one-way NDA?
- Any required firewall/VPC allowlist entries for the Dedicated trial?

Next steps (if you agree):
- Ibrahim to confirm dataset availability and NDA by 5/31.
- We'll provision the Dedicated trial slot and share a setup checklist (internal owners listed below).

Owners:
- Customer data & eval questions: Ibrahim + NovaDocs Eval Team
- Redwood setup & infra: Marissa (trial lead) + Sean (infrastructure)
- Evaluation tooling & offline harness: Alex Martinez

I attached a short spreadsheet with suggested evaluation questions and a checklist (NovaDocs-Eval-Questions.xlsx). If this looks good, I’ll schedule the kickoff for Monday.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: NovaDocs-Eval-Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet of proposed labels / eval cases), Signed-NDA-NovaDocs.pdf (placeholder for NDA to be sent)

From: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@novadocs.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, NovaDocs Evaluation Team <eval@novadocs.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial playbook and evaluation framework — Redwood / NovaDocs

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. We’re aligned on the high level. Quick answers and some clarifications below: 

1) Dataset: We can deliver a 12k anonymized sample (export via S3 link) by COB Monday (5/31). It will include the labels you requested but note that ~6% are edge cases with overlapping labels.
2) NDA: Legal approved the one-way NDA; I’ve attached the signed PDF (Signed-NDA-NovaDocs.pdf).
3) Firewall: Our infra team will provide IPs for allowlist; expect that by Monday morning.

Success criteria tweaks from our side: 
- Please add recall-min per class (no class lower than 0.85 recall) — we need to avoid systematic misses.
- For latency, can we capture both median and 95th percentile while simulating our short burst profile (10 concurrent callers for 30s every 5 minutes)?

Evaluation approach preference: we’d like an offline-first evaluation to validate quality metrics quickly, then move to an online shadow (if metrics look good) to validate latency and real-world behavior. Would prefer the shadow to run against a 7-day sample of anonymized traffic if possible.

I’ll loop in our Eval Team separately with the dataset S3 link.

— Ibrahim
Ibrahim Khan | Head of Product 
NovaDocs
ibrahim.khan@novadocs.ai | +1 (650) 555-2134

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@novadocs.ai>, NovaDocs Evaluation Team <eval@novadocs.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial playbook and evaluation framework — Redwood / NovaDocs

Thanks Ibrahim — this is helpful. Below is a concrete, pragmatic evaluation methodology that maps to your offline-first preference and then the shadow run. Please review and flag anything missing.

Evaluation plan (detailed):
A) Offline evaluation (Day 1–4 of trial run) — purpose: validate quality and iterate quickly.
- Inputs: your anonymized 12k sample (train/test split already applied by you; we will use the evaluation partition).
- Steps: run Redwood inference on the eval partition, produce per-document predictions + confidence scores, and produce per-label confusion matrices.
- Metrics to report: precision, recall, F1 per class; macro F1; PHI-redaction false negative rate; calibration (Brier score) for critical labels.
- Acceptance gates (pass->continue to shadow): macro F1 >= 0.92 AND no class with recall < 0.85 AND PHI-redaction FNR <= 0.005.

B) Shadow run (optional, Day 8–10) — purpose: validate latency, caching, and safety under realistic traffic.
- Setup: mirror a representative 72–168h window (your choice) of anonymized traffic to a Redwood Dedicated endpoint in read-only mode; traffic will not be surfaced to end users.
- Observability: collect per-request latency (P50/P95/P99), payload sizes, batching behavior, and KV cache hit ratio.
- Safety checks: run a random sample of outputs through your internal PHI detection and run our secondary redaction verification. Any PHI misses must be logged and reviewed within 24h.

Grading rubric (example scoring, scale 0–5):
- Label accuracy (macro F1): 5 = >=0.95, 4 = 0.92–0.949, 3 = 0.88–0.919, 2 = 0.80–0.879, 1 = <0.80
- PHI redaction (FNR): 5 = <=0.001, 4 = <=0.003, 3 = <=0.005, 2 = <=0.01, 1 = >0.01
- Latency (P50/P95): 5 = P50<=200ms & P95<=600ms, 4 = P50<=300ms & P95<=800ms, 3 = P50<=350ms & P95<=900ms, 2 = P50<=500ms, 1 = P50>500ms
- Stability / errors: 5 = 0 runtime errors, 4 = <=0.01% errors, 3 = <=0.1% errors, 2 = <=0.5% errors, 1 = >0.5%

Decision matrix: to proceed to production consideration, we need average rubric score >= 4 across the four axes above and zero PHI critical misses during the shadow run.

Operational notes and ownership:
- Redwood provides the evaluation harness and will produce a post-trial report within 3 business days of trial end (Owner: Alex Martinez).
- Dedicated slot and infra tuning: Sean Gallagher (Owner). Please confirm GPU sizing: default proposal T4x2; if your traffic sim suggests N1 or larger we’ll adjust.
- Data handling and legal questions: Ibrahim + NovaDocs legal. Redwood will not persist raw documents beyond 30 days, per the NDA.

Proposed timeline:
- Mon 5/31: dataset + allowlist + signed NDA (you) -> Redwood provisions slot (Marissa/Sean).
- Tue 6/1: baseline run + offline eval kicks off.
- Tue 6/8: optional shadow window (if offline gates pass).
- Fri 6/11: delivery of final post-trial report.

If you’re aligned I’ll post a calendar invite for the Mon 5/31 kickoff and open the infra ticket for allowlist entries.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Marissa
